subject.title: feat(ui): logo-scare lobster visits; drop the model-auth-expiring chip

question: Should OpenClaw remove the sidebar warning for every provider reported as `expiring`, or retain a differentiated warning for expiry states that require user action?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes the user-facing auth-notification policy rather than correcting a defined broken contract, and the supplied evidence does not establish that all expiring states are harmless rolling OAuth expiry.

options.title: Retain actionable expiry warnings
options.body: Keep or refine the warning so providers with a user-actionable expiry continue to alert, while suppressing only proven continuously refreshed OAuth states.

options.title: Remove the warning globally
options.body: Accept the reduced early-warning signal and rely on the existing expired-auth error as the sole sidebar notification.

recommendation.title: Retain actionable expiry warnings
recommendation.body: Keep or refine the warning so providers with a user-actionable expiry continue to alert, while suppressing only proven continuously refreshed OAuth states.
